title: AI Risk Management Framework
explain_beginner: This paper presents an optional framework from NIST for handling dangers from AI. It is meant for groups that create, launch, or operate AI. The framework is designed to be flexible, not tied to one industry or one kind of use, and suitable for organizations of different sizes. It aims to support reliable and accountable AI while protecting people from possible harms. It also is meant to be useful in practice and able to change as AI technology changes. In short, it gives organizations a shared way to think about AI risks, though following it is a choice, not a legal requirement.
explain_business: This framework gives executives an optional, flexible way to handle AI dangers across creation, launch, operation, and use. It is not limited to one sector or one kind of use, so it can fit organizations of different sizes and capacities. It aims to support reliable and accountable AI while lowering possible harms, and it is meant to change as AI changes. In practice, it informs decisions about AI oversight, risk handling, and client or internal alignment claims. Because clients may say they follow this NIST framework, an audit should test those claims against the framework rather than accept them at face value.
explain_practitioner: This work introduces the AI Risk Management Framework, created under the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020. It offers a resource for teams that create, launch, or operate AI systems, helping them handle AI dangers and encourage reliable, accountable use. The framework is optional, aims to protect rights, is not tied to a sector, and is not limited to one kind of use. It is intended to be useful in practice, able to change as AI develops, and implementable to different degrees depending on an organization's capacity. The key result is a flexible structure for risk management rather than a fixed checklist. Audits may test alignment claims against it.
